ABSTRACT Although face‐centered cubic high‐entropy alloys (HEAs) have received extensive attention and in‐depth research, most existing studies focus on single temperature or strain rate conditions, lacking systematic investigations into deformation mechanisms under extreme thermomechanical coupling environments. In this work, a CoCrFeNiTi 0.2 HEA containing ultrafine L1 2 precipitates and η phases was fabricated, and compression tests were performed over a wide range of temperatures (293–1273 K) and strain rates (0.001–5000 s −1 ), followed by systematic characterization of the corresponding microstructural evolution. The results demonstrate an inverse thermal softening behavior at various strain rates. Anomalous double‐humped stress peaks, separately induced by third‐type strain aging and in situ coarsening of L1 2 precipitates during deformation, were observed in the flow stress–temperature curves, leading to the inverse thermal softening behavior. The stress peak associated with third‐type strain aging appears at various strain rates and shifts toward higher temperatures with increasing strain rate. Ti atoms serve as solute atoms, forming solute atmospheres and effectively pinning mobile dislocations. In contrast, the other stress peak induced by in situ coarsening of L1 2 precipitates is nearly insensitive to strain rate. The dependence of multiple deformation mechanisms—including dislocation slip, twinning, stacking fault‐mediated plasticity, and dynamic recrystallization—on temperature and strain rate was thoroughly investigated. Finally, a schematic diagram of deformation mechanisms covering the entire investigated temperature and strain rate range was constructed. This study elucidates the deformation mechanisms of the CoCrFeNiTi 0.2 HEA in extreme environments, offering an important theoretical basis and experimental support for the design and application of high‐performance HEAs in aerospace, weaponry, and other fields. 公开阅读反馈 暂缓自动推荐: https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Modification+of+the+Johnson-Cook+constitutive+model+for+34CrNi3MoA+alloy+steel+based+on+th&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1117%2F12.3125323%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22temperature%22%2C+%22strain_rate%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 This work examines the high-rate compression response of 34CrNi3MoA alloy steel by means of SHPB tests carried out at 25 °C, 200 °C, 400 °C and 600 °C, with strain rates ranging from 1000 to 4600 s⁻¹. The experimental curves indicate rate strengthening, thermal softening and a local stress increase related to dynamic strain aging in a specific temperature rate interval. When the conventional Johnson-Cook model was calibrated with the same data set, the average relative error reached 20.63%, showing that the separable strain, rate and temperature terms were insufficient for this material. To improve the description, the model was revised by introducing a rate-dependent thermal-softening exponent, a two dimensional Gaussian function for the dynamic-strain-aging peak and a hardening coefficient coupled with both temperature and strain rate. The revised model reduced the average relative error to 2.88% and gave a closer representation of the measured curves within the tested range. The proposed equation is therefore recommended as an interpolation model for 1000-4600 s⁻¹ and 25-600 °C; application beyond this domain still requires further calibration and uncertainty evaluation. Published: 2026-09-30T00:00:00+00:00 Venue: Twelfth International Conference on Mechanical Engineering, Materials, and Automation Technology (MMEAT 2026) 研究类型: 跨金属方法参考

Accurate constitutive modeling of hot deformation characteristics is essential for the development of thermomechanical procedures for advanced structural alloys. Conventional Arrhenius-type and empirical models frequently find it challenging to effectively depict the combined influences of strain hardening, dynamic recovery (DRV), and dynamic recrystallization (DRX) across extensive processing intervals. This research uses two Stacked Residual Physics-Informed Neural Networks (STAR-PINNs) to predict the hot-deformation characteristics of a Mo-rich α + β titanium alloy (Ti–6Al–4Mo–1V–0.1Si). The Improved STAR-PINN integrates thermomechanical constitutive restrictions, while the DRX-Aware STAR-PINN utilizes a dual-output framework that incorporates recrystallization kinetics through a trainable JMAK–Avrami model. Both models utilize a common residual encoder that is trained on empirical flow-stress data collected at temperatures ranging from 800 to 1050 °C and strain rates between 0.01 and 10 s⁻¹ . Constraints informed by physics that enforce thermal softening, strain-rate sensitivity, strain hardening, and post-peak softening are applied via automatic differentiation. The DRX-Aware model also includes JMAK–Avrami regularization featuring learnable, constrained kinetic parameters k and n, DRX saturation limits, Arrhenius-based consistency, and latent-feature integration connecting the estimated DRX fraction to the stress output. The DRX-Aware STAR-PINN obtained RMSE = 11.62 MPa, MAE = 4.73 MPa, and R² = 0.9852 on the test set reserved for validation, along with a five-fold cross-validated RMSE of 12.74 ± 0.38 MPa. The learned JMAK parameters converged to k = 2.03 and n = 1.99 , remaining close to the conventional values while being inferred directly from the data. The model effectively mirrored flow curves influenced by temperature, DRX development, and Zener–Hollomon correlations under interpolation scenarios while preserving physically coherent constitutive behavior. These findings illustrate that physics-informed deep learning delivers a precise and understandable structure for constitutive modeling, presenting a viable approach for sophisticated process modeling of hot-deformed titanium alloys. item.title: Efficient GA–BP-assisted calibration of a semi-coupled damage framework for thin QP980 steel sheets using limited experimental data
item.description: 库内相似论文：Hybrid identification method of coupled viscoplastic-damage constitutive parameters based on BP neural network and genetic algorithm（相似度 0.707） 引用重点论文：Application of extended Mohr–Coulomb criterion to ductile fracture [https://doi.org/10.1007/s10704-009-9422-8] 引用重点论文：A new model of metal plasticity and fracture with pressure and Lode dependence [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijplas.2007.09.004] 与《Fracture of laser powder bed fusion additively manufactured Ti–6Al–4V under multiaxial loading: Calibration and comparison of fracture models》共享 6 篇参考文献；归一化重合度 0.129 共享参考文献示例：https://openalex.org/W2032768430, https://openalex.org/W2048598423, https://openalex.org/W2065163759, https://openalex.org/W2086827153, https://openalex.org/W2086998939 复杂应力状态与屈服准则: 可作为屈服面形式、压力/Lode 依赖与试样构型设计的比较线索（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对应力状态覆盖范围、是否含负三轴度、加载路径是否比例 摘要片段: The plastic response is described by … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知 塑性变形与硬化律: 可作为硬化律选型与颈缩后外推方案的参考（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对标定应变范围、外推是否有独立验证、是否混用不同试样 摘要片段: The plastic response is described by … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知 摘要方法线索: Mohr-Coulomb, MMC, Hill48 https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Efficient+GA%E2%80%93BP-assisted+calibration+of+a+semi-coupled+damage+framework+for+thin+QP980+ste&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.matdes.2026.116960%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22stress_state%22%2C+%22plasticity_hardening%22%2C+%22ductile_fracture%22%2C+%22damage_evolution%22%2C+%22calibration%22%2C+%22other_metals%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Efficient calibration of damage-evolution parameters remains a key challenge in semi-coupled fracture modeling of advanced high-strength steels because these parameters are not directly measurable and usually require repeated experiment–simulation iterations. This study develops a semi-coupled damage framework for thin QP980 steel sheets under limited experimental data. The plastic response is described by the Hill48 yield criterion and a modified Swift–Voce hardening law, damage initiation by a Modified Mohr–Coulomb (MMC)-based fracture locus, and post-initiation softening by a continuum damage mechanics (CDM)-based evolution law. A hierarchical calibration strategy is adopted: plasticity and damage-initiation parameters are determined through conventional experiment–simulation procedures, whereas damage-evolution parameters are identified using a genetic algorithm–backpropagation (GA-BP) neural network. A finite element database was constructed from the R5 notched specimen, with parameter ranges selected to cover the observed softening response. The calibrated framework was validated using notched and shear specimens. The GA–BP-calibrated model reproduced experimental force–displacement curves and fracture displacements, with fracture displacement errors within 3.4%. Digital image correlation (DIC) strain-field comparisons further confirmed the predicted localization patterns. The results provide an efficient, physically constrained route for semi-coupled damage-model calibration and fracture assessment of thin QP980 steel sheets. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Predicting+stress%E2%80%93strain+behaviors+of+additively+manufactured+materials+via+loss-based+and&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.aei.2026.105322%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22lpbf_tc4%22%2C+%22strain_rate%22%2C+%22plasticity_hardening%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Predicting the stress–strain behaviors of additively manufactured materials is crucial for part qualification in additive manufacturing (AM). Conventional physics-based constitutive models of materials have limitations, such as oversimplification of material properties and narrow applicability to limited strain rates, while purely data-driven machine learning (ML) models often lack physical consistency and interpretability. To address these issues, we introduce a physics-informed machine learning (PIML) framework that leverages physical laws in elastic and plastic regions to improve the predictive performance and physical consistency when predicting the stress–strain curves of additively manufactured polymers and metals. A polynomial regression model is first used to predict the yield point based on AM process parameters, and then the stress–strain curves are segmented into elastic and plastic regions using the predicted yield point. Two long short-term memory (LSTM) models are trained to predict the two regions separately. For the elastic region, Hooke’s law is embedded in the LSTM models for both polymers and metals. For the plastic region, Voce hardening law and Hollomon’s law are embedded in the LSTM models for the polymers and metals, respectively. In addition, the PIML framework is implemented by two architectures, including the loss-based and activation-based PIML architectures, where the physical laws are embedded into the loss and activation functions, respectively. The performance of the two PIML architectures is compared with two LSTM-based ML models, three additional ML models, including a ridge polynomial regression model, an artificial neural network, and a transformer, and a physics-based constitutive model. These models are built on experimental data collected from two additively manufactured polymers (i.e., Nylon and carbon fiber-acrylonitrile butadiene styrene) and two additively manufactured metals (i.e., AlSi10Mg and Ti6Al4V). Experimental results demonstrate that two PIML architectures consistently outperform other ML baseline models and the physics-based constitutive model. The segmental predictive model with the activation-based PIML architecture achieves the best overall performance, with the lowest MAPE of 10.46 ± 0.81 %, the lowest MAE of 26.07 ± 2.52 MPa, the lowest RMSE of 29.28 ± 2.83 MPa, and the highest R 2 of 0.82 ± 0.05, indicating superior predictive performance for four different materials. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Dynamic+constitutive+model+of+hydrogen-resistant+steel+based+on+isothermal+true+stress-str&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.jmrt.2026.09.062%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22temperature%22%2C+%22strain_rate%22%2C+%22plasticity_hardening%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Hydrogen-resistant steel is an important engineering material for core components in advanced weapon systems and nuclear physics experiments because of its high strength, high toughness, and excellent resistance to hydrogen embrittlement under high-temperature and high-pressure conditions. In this study, a high-temperature Split Hopkinson pressure bar (SHPB) system was used to characterize the dynamic mechanical response of hydrogen-resistant steel. True stress–strain curves were obtained under different strains, strain rates, and deformation temperatures. The results show that the true stress exhibits nonlinear strain-hardening behavior, while thermal softening causes it to decrease with increasing deformation temperature. The adiabatic temperature rise during plastic deformation was calculated by considering the temperature dependence of the specific heat capacity. The actual deformation temperatures were then determined, and the true stress–strain curves obtained under non-isothermal conditions were corrected to isothermal true stress–strain curves using a thermal-softening coefficient. Based on the corrected isothermal true stress–strain curves, Power-Law and Johnson–Cook constitutive models were established for hydrogen-resistant steel. The established models were fitted to the SHPB-derived isothermal true stress–strain data and assessed through two-dimensional cutting simulations. They captured the main cutting-force trends under the tested conditions, although deviations increased at high cutting speeds. Thus, the models may serve as phenomenological inputs for preliminary cutting simulations within the investigated range. The prediction of microstructural characteristics during the deformation of metals has consistently been a key area of research. Previous studies have shown that ultrasonic vibration-assisted riveting experimentally produces quantitative changes in grain size (GS) and geometrically necessary dislocation (GND) density of rivets. However, existing microscale theoretical models predominantly focus on the prediction of total dislocation density. Moreover, most established models are developed for longitudinal ultrasonic vibration, while few studies have addressed the quantitative prediction of GS and GND density of microstructural characteristics during transverse ultrasonic vibration-assisted forming. Therefore, this study focused on 2A10 aluminum alloy specimens, which are widely used in aviation. Transverse ultrasonic vibration-assisted compression (TUVAC) tests were performed under different ultrasonic amplitudes. Based on the experimental investigation, a multiscale ultrasonic constitutive model incorporating GND density and GS was established, and a VUMAT subroutine was developed to predict the microstructural characteristics of the 2A10 aluminum alloy in TUVAC simulations. The results indicated that the maximum flow stress decreased from 509.7 MPa to 477.4 MPa as the ultrasonic amplitude increased from 0 μm to 21.2 μm. Compared to the original specimen, the intensity of the < 111>||ND fiber texture decreased significantly after simple compression. When transverse ultrasonic vibration was applied during compression, the Copper texture continuously weakened and the Brass texture gradually strengthened with increasing ultrasonic amplitude. In contrast, both the S texture and the < 111>||ND fiber texture initially increased and then decreased. GND density increased nonlinearly while the GS gradually decreased, indicating significant grain refinement. The predicted results of the ultrasonic constitutive model were compared with experimental data. This comparison showed that the average absolute relative error (AARE) for stress remained below 2.2 % under different amplitudes. A comparative analysis of experimental and simulation results revealed that the maximum AARE was approximately 15 % for GND density, approximately 12 % for GS, and below 5 % for microhardness. Thus, the proposed constitutive model can accurately predict both macroscopic mechanical behavior and microstructural characteristics and thereby provides a solid theoretical foundation for further investigation into the micro-mechanisms and performance of ultrasonic-assisted riveting. This article evaluates the adequacy of the constitutive models proposed in the literature by comparing the results of terminal ballistics computer simulations with available experimental data on the penetration of armour steel by an armour-piercing projectile. The simulations use a modified Johnson-Cook model, enhanced by using the Cockcroft-Latham ductile fracture criterion rather than a standard failure model. The analysis includes a mesh structure as well as the algorithm for interaction between elements. Mesh-convergence tests were performed to assess the effect of mesh density on the modelling results. Based on our own mechanical tests of core material properties, the analysis indicates the need for improved constitutive model calibration. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Microstructure-informed+decoupling+and+machine-learning+prediction+of+hole+expansion+behav&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.jmrt.2026.09.173%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22stress_state%22%2C+%22other_metals%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 The hole expansion ratio (HER) of advanced high-strength steels is governed by both intrinsic edge formability and punched-hole edge conditions. However, directly quantifying the punching effect is difficult owing to the influence of interacting variables and severely deformed localized regions. Extending the previous decoupling of HER into intrinsic edge formability (HER 0 , defined as the HER of an electrical discharge machined hole) and punching-induced HER degradation (ΔHER, defined as the relative decrease from HER 0 to the HER of a punched-hole) this study establishes simpler surrogate indicators for these two contributions. Uniaxial tensile and shear tests were conducted to capture HER 0 and ΔHER, respectively. Finite element simulations revealed that the punching process and shear test showed a similar low-stress triaxiality deformation state in the localized deformation region. Micro-hardness profiling confirmed the comparable work hardening behaviors of the two processes. The proposed framework was experimentally validated using two hot-rolled martensitic steel types with an identical chemical composition but different rolling reduction ratios. Notably, the steel with a higher HER 0 exhibited a lower punched-hole HER because of its larger ΔHER, demonstrating that ΔHER can reverse the HER performance. Microstructural analyses indicated that the prior austenite grain size affected carbide precipitation, leading to opposite HER 0 and ΔHER trends. Finally, a two-stage machine-learning-based HER prediction model incorporating parameters derived from uniaxial tensile and shear tests accurately predicted HER 0 and HER achieving high R 2 values. These results establish a surrogate-test-based framework for predicting HER by separately considering the intrinsic material response and process-induced hole edge conditions. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Lattice+reconstruction+and+dislocation+recapture+enhance+the+fracture+resistance+of+%CE%B7-Fe2A&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1088%2F2631-7990%2Faeab39%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22temperature%22%2C+%22umat_implementation%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Abstract The inherent brittleness of interfacial Al-rich intermetallic compounds (IMCs) remains a major obstacle to reliable Fe-Al-based light-structural joints, as welding-induced residual-stress localization readily triggers crack initiation within the IMC-bearing region. Here, a two-step strategy integrating lattice reconstruction with dislocation recapture is proposed to improve the room-temperature fracture resistance of η-Fe2Al5 in Al/steel dissimilar joints. Low-temperature annealing promotes rapid reconstruction of the strained η-Fe2Al5 lattice and relieves long-range residual stress, while subsequent water quenching facilitates the recapture of dispersed isolated dislocations. The treated joints achieve a tensile strength of ~258.6 MPa, corresponding to an ~80.3% increase over the as-processed state, together with a ~70% increase in the fracture toughness of the η-Fe2Al5-bearing layer. In-situ X-ray diffraction and first-principles calculations reveal that localized compressive strain accelerates the reverse eutectoid transformation, through which β0-associated transformation strain provides an additional driving force for dislocation-network decoupling and stress relief. The retained coherent η-Fe2Al5/β0 interface and the recaptured isolated dislocations further promote local strain accommodation in η-Fe2Al5, while crack deflection, blunting, and bridging dissipate fracture energy, as supported by molecular dynamics simulations. These results suggest a potential strategy for improving fracture-limited IMC-bearing interfaces in dissimilar-metal joints through coordinated regulation of residual stress and dislocation functionality. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+Sub-10-nm+stacking+bands+enable+ultrastrong+additively+manufactured+titanium&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1038%2Fs41563-026-02749-6%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22lpbf_tc4%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 Lightweight alloys with superior strength–ductility synergies are crucial for advanced structural applications, and nanostructured titanium (Ti) alloys are promising candidates. However, it remains challenging to manufacture bulk components with complex geometries as well as preserving the nanostructure and associated excellent mechanical properties. Here we report an ultrastrong Ti alloy fabricated by laser powder bed fusion, with composition and processing parameters optimized using the high-throughput experiments and machine learning method. This route yields a microstructure consisting of sub-10-nm stacking bands driven by martensitic transformation within a previously inaccessible composition–processing regime. This nanostructured microstructure endows the Ti alloy with a yield strength of ~1.5 GPa, an ultimate tensile strength exceeding 1.7 GPa, uniform elongation of ~7.5% and specific strength of ~380 MPa cm3 g‒1. The developed Ti alloy combines high strength, ductility and scalable manufacturing, offering a promising combination of properties for structural applications. Integrating laser powder bed fusion with a high-throughput screening and machine learning method identifies a processing–composition regime for fabricating Ti alloys with sub-10-nm stacking bands, which present high specific strength and potential for scalable manufacturing. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+A+Machine+Learning+Model+for+AA7075-T6+Based+on+Anisotropic+Elastoplastic+Constitutive+The&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.3390%2Fma19194165%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22stress_state%22%2C+%22plasticity_hardening%22%2C+%22umat_implementation%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 In this study, a machine learning model for the anisotropic mechanical behavior of AA7075-T6 was successfully developed by combining classical plasticity theory with neural network algorithms. First, a yield criterion incorporating strength asymmetry and orientation dependence was constructed based on a fourth-order linear transformation of invariants, and a stress update algorithm was implemented using the return mapping and implicit integration schemes. Subsequently, a dataset comprising experimental results from tension, compression, and shear tests at multiple orientations, as well as theoretically generated data from additional strain paths, was established to train a genetic algorithm-optimized two-hidden-layer neural network. Plastic-stage assessments indicated that, for the equal-biaxial path, the RMSE values of the stress–strain curves predicted by the machine learning model relative to the constitutive implementation were 31.87 and 39.24 MPa. It should be noted that the stress–strain response under equal-biaxial loading represents an additional prediction case. The trained model exhibited satisfactory predictive performance when compared against experimental data for tension, compression, and shear and was capable of reproducing the theoretical stress paths derived from the classical constitutive model. This approach leverages the physical interpretability of conventional constitutive modeling and the high efficiency of data-driven methods, providing a viable solution for efficiently predicting the anisotropic mechanical response of metallic materials under complex stress states. Abstract Auxetic lattices are an important part in the development of smart metamaterials suitable for intelligent applications in high strain-rate dynamics. In this work, three types of auxetic lattices (missing-rib, two- and three-dimensional re-entrant honeycomb) additively manufactured from 316L stainless steel using the LPBF method were subjected to a combined experimental and numerical investigation of their compressive response under quasi-static conditions and during dynamic impact at nominal strain rates of $$1500{\text {s}^{-1}}$$ and $$3000{\text {s}^{-1}}$$ in an in-house designed SHPB apparatus. All the experiments were instrumented using optical cameras for non-contact deformation tracking to establish deformation fields in the samples and calculate the strain and strain-rate dependent function of Poisson’s ratio. A fully 3D three-bar finite element model of the SHPB apparatus and the studied lattices was developed and implemented in LS-DYNA. Mesh density and discretization type sensitivity studies were carried out together with the experimental calibration of strain-rate dependent bilinear constitutive model representing the material of the 3D printed lattices. Simulated dynamic impacts were performed with the same initial conditions as the experiments and the numerical stress-strain characteristics of the studied samples were calculated from the numerical strain signals using the same mathematical methods used for evaluation of laboratory SHPB experiments. The agreement of the experimental and simulated stress-strain response up to the densification region was studied for all the investigated types of lattices at both dynamic strain rates. To interpret the origin of the discrepancies in the simulated and observed stress-strain response as well as the calculated function of Poisson’s ratio, X-ray computed microtomographical imaging was performed and the assessed differences were attributed to the manufacturing inaccuracies and defects in the samples. Abstract Body-centered cubic (BCC) metals often exhibit limited ductility at finite temperatures, and elemental synergy in multi-principal element alloys (MPEAs) offers a promising route to overcome this limitation. Here, we employ atomistic simulations with a high fidelity machine-learning potential—which outperforms traditional empirical potentials at capturing complex chemical interactions—to investigate mode-I crack propagation in the engineering-relevant NbMoTaW MPEA versus pure Mo. While Mo fails by brittle cleavage, the NbMoTaW undergoes ductile fracture mediated by dislocation activity. We demonstrate that the average-based Rice criterion demands local corrections to sample diverse chemical environments along the advancing crack. Specifically, the MPEA's intrinsic chemo-mechanical heterogeneity produces atomic-scale stress delocalization at the crack tip, generating a chemically-driven shielding effect that mitigates the singular stress concentration responsible for cleavage. In particular, Ta-related local chemical heterogeneities act as precursors that nucleate localized shear and dissipate plastic energy. By embedding such heterogeneities into a brittle Mo matrix, we demonstrate that a sufficient level of interconnectivity is required to amplify stress delocalization and promote dislocation nucleation, enabling a brittle-to-ductile transition of the fracture mode. These findings reveal a stress delocalization mechanism by which local chemical heterogeneities control intrinsic ductility in BCC alloys and provide a theoretical guide for composition design. https://github.com/lwz20210407/ZotWatch/issues/new?title=%5BZotWatch+feedback%5D+%E6%9A%82%E7%BC%93%E8%87%AA%E5%8A%A8%E6%8E%A8%E8%8D%90+A+hybrid+data-driven+J2-based+plasticity+model+for+plastic+anisotropy+evolution+in+metals&body=%3C%21--+zotwatch-feedback-v2+--%3E%0A%60%60%60json%0A%7B%22doi%22%3A+%2210.1016%2Fj.matdes.2026.117079%22%2C+%22rating%22%3A+%22later%22%2C+%22facets%22%3A+%5B%22plasticity_hardening%22%5D%2C+%22reason%22%3A+%22%22%2C+%22applicability%22%3A+%22hold%22%7D%0A%60%60%60%0A%E5%85%AC%E5%BC%80%E5%8F%8D%E9%A6%88%EF%BC%8C%E8%AF%B7%E5%8B%BF%E5%A1%AB%E5%86%99%E7%A7%81%E4%BA%BA%E7%AC%94%E8%AE%B0%E3%80%82 This study proposes a plasticity framework for describing anisotropic hardening and flow direction evolution, which employs data-driven concepts to enhance the traditional von Mises plasticity framework. The approach is an alternative to advanced anisotropic phenomenological plasticity models. On one hand, it incorporates all available data within the experimentally investigated loading path domain into the constitutive plastic response, unlike the traditional models which only use a limited part of the data. On the other hand, it defaults to standard isotropic J2 plastic flow outside of the investigated domain, without making unbased extrapolations of the plastic flow direction far into the untested loading paths. The hardening response is represented using an artificial neural network trained on stress–strain data obtained from different loading directions. Simultaneously, a plastic flow corrector reproduces the experimentally measured r-value evolution. The performance of proposed framework was assessed through finite element simulations of tensile specimens and compared against a conventional Voce hardening model calibrated using a single material orientation. The best agreement with experiments is achieved before the onset of necking, while larger deviations occur under the complex stress states that develop during post-necking deformation. The study demonstrates a thermodynamically admissible framework for modeling highly anisotropic plastic deformation. Published: 2026-09-18T00:00:00+00:00 Venue: Materials & Design 研究类型: 跨金属方法参考

item.title: An anisotropic constitutive model for forming of aluminum tubes under both biaxial tension and pure shear stress states
item.description: 经典文献补漏 库内相似论文：Anisotropic plasticity model forms for extruded al 7079: Part II, validation（相似度 0.843） 被相关论文引用：An asymmetric yield criterion for plasticity modeling of metal sheets considering shear and near-plane strain tension [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jmrt.2026.09.163] 与《A lode-dependent plasticity model for high-strength structural steel》共享 5 篇参考文献；归一化重合度 0.111 共享参考文献示例：https://openalex.org/W1969052431, https://openalex.org/W2047824887, https://openalex.org/W2757592523, https://openalex.org/W2945042196, https://openalex.org/W2972543083 复杂应力状态与屈服准则: 可作为屈服面形式、压力/Lode 依赖与试样构型设计的比较线索（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对应力状态覆盖范围、是否含负三轴度、加载路径是否比例 仅题名片段: An anisotropic constitutive model for forming … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知 其他金属的同链研究: 研究链一致时与钛合金同等参考价值；建模思路、标定流程与验证方案可直接借鉴（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对材料体系差异与微观机制是否可比；参数量级不可直接套用，需在 TC4 上重新标定 仅题名片段: An anisotropic constitutive model for forming … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知 公开阅读反馈 直接有用: item.title: Ductile fracture prediction using enhanced CDM model with Lode angle-dependency for titanium alloy Ti-6Al-4V at room temperature
item.description: 经典文献补漏 库内相似论文：Enhanced CDM model accounting of stress triaxiality and lode angle for ductile damage prediction in metal forming（相似度 0.800） 引用重点论文：A new model of metal plasticity and fracture with pressure and Lode dependence [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ijplas.2007.09.004] 被相关论文引用：Ductile fracture model describing the impact of internal pores: Model development and validation for additively manufactured Ti-6Al-4V [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.addma.2025.104722] 与《Fracture of laser powder bed fusion additively manufactured Ti–6Al–4V under multiaxial loading: Calibration and comparison of fracture models》共享 5 篇参考文献；归一化重合度 0.121 共享参考文献示例：https://openalex.org/W1977188519, https://openalex.org/W2048598423, https://openalex.org/W2086827153, https://openalex.org/W2086998939, https://openalex.org/W2157258353 复杂应力状态与屈服准则: 可作为屈服面形式、压力/Lode 依赖与试样构型设计的比较线索（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对应力状态覆盖范围、是否含负三轴度、加载路径是否比例 摘要片段: Lode angle-dependent enhanced fully coupled damage … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知 损伤演化与孔洞机制: 可作为损伤累积形式与孔洞机制建模的参考（规则推断，非已验证迁移） 迁移前检查: 核对损伤变量定义、是否与塑性耦合、单元尺寸依赖是否处理 摘要片段: Lode angle-dependent enhanced fully coupled damage … 标题/摘要不能确认全部实验条件与方法适用性，未陈述内容保持未知 摘要方法线索: VUMAT 采用方法线索；摘要句子层面的规则线索，不等同于对某篇被引论文的评价 公开阅读反馈 直接有用: Fully coupled ductile damage model considering strength-differential (SD) effect is proposed for simulation of metal forming processes for Ti-6Al-4V. The developed constitutive equations are based on non-associative plasticity theory under thermodynamically-consistent framework. The third stress invariant is added to Hill48 criterion to capture the SD effect. Lode angle-dependent enhanced fully coupled damage model is proposed to account for the loading path sensitivity on ductile damage initiation and growth. A detailed material parameters identification procedure is presented. The proposed model is implemented into the FE code Abaqus/Explicit through user defined subroutine VUMAT. The numerically predicted results obtained with the proposed model are compared to experimental data of Ti-6Al-4V and good agreement is observed.
